abstract: The integration of genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with single-cell RNA sequencing has enabled the dissection of complex trait architectures across tissue-resolved cellular contexts. However, existing resources lack the ability to identify hub genes underlying trait-cell-type associations, dissect gene-gene interaction topologies, or detect shared genes across multiple traits. Here, we present single-cell-assisted Genome-Wide Association Study DataBase (scGWAS-DB) (https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/scgwasdb), an integrated database that bridges population-scale genetics with single-cell biology. scGWAS-DB integrates 3,649 high-quality GWAS datasets with single-cell atlases spanning 74 human tissues and 1,713 cell types. From these data, we identified 213,992 significant triplets, encompassing 821,480 gene-gene interactions. Among them, we further distinguished 584,944 co-occurrent and 7,365 mutual exclusive gene-gene interaction patterns. Systematic integration of these networks revealed recurrent cellular signatures across diverse diseases. Collectively, scGWAS-DB provides a systematic resource for interpreting the cellular basis of complex traits, prioritizing hub genes and cell types that could provide insights in future studies of drug target development and disease-relevant cellular circuit discovery.
